phase1.instructions: Use only the tools returned by tools/list. Follow the installed phase-one production skills. Read the selected project and current content version before editing. Save native source through kinevyn_edit_project; preview and export perform their required checks internally. Use kinevyn_list_versions to find project snapshots and kinevyn_restore_version to restore one as a new version while retaining later history. A transport cancellation does not prove a background export stopped. Report actual export state and accessible results; technical validation does not replace visual, audio and player review. Never guess a project from another conversation. Read skills locally or with resources/list and resources/read (kinevyn://workflow/production/start, or the selected specialist); engine authoring guidance is kinevyn://engine/SKILL.md and relative Markdown references under kinevyn://engine/. For new work create explicitly; kinevyn_open_preview never silently creates a project. Use kinevyn_open_preview target=templates for the editor template library without any project/session/version binding; browse first and create only after user selection. Follow its page handoff, without a project record_display receipt. Persisted create/import/edit/restore/export/cancel and review requests require a stable requestId; preview action=open does not. Edits require projectId, expectedRevision and expectedVersionId. Query export progress through kinevyn_get_project with projectId and exportJobId. Project list and version list are five per page; follow nextCursor. For template discovery, call kinevyn_list_templates to obtain a local JSONL index path, then search that file with local tools. It does not return search results. Read candidate IDs with kinevyn_get_template. Only an explicit request to use a selected editable template authorizes kinevyn_create_project projectType=template; a recommendation request alone does not. Use the connected Kinevyn MCP tools for project operations and exports; a shell HTTP call is not an MCP tool invocation. Before opening a project, verify the connection dataDirectory and project/version with kinevyn_get_project. Browser URLs and project IDs do not select another workspace. Compatible phase-one plugin/backend updates continue automatically on the existing connection through API protocol and Tool negotiation; keep the workspace, project binding and running exports. If the API is incompatible, update the incompatible components together when idle. Only an already-closed host transport or an internal legacy runtime replacement requires reconnection. Do not silently bypass MCP or change workspaces. After the final video is ready to preview (or an explicit editor-only request), follow previewHandoff and production/native#continuing-edits to request the latest preview in the calling chat. Default foreground preserves the current chat: queue while inactive, then resolve the latest project version on return. Bind the actual native providerTabId, synchronize Codex IAB visibility without navigation, and independently verify settled visibility and changed live content. Record action=record_display only for the observed revision/version; queued alone is not confirmation or proof that the calling chat is inactive. Complete the same visibility checks for first delivery. Hidden automation tabs, markDeliverable and MP4 export do not satisfy editor delivery. Use visibility=queued only for confirmed inactive-chat deferral; otherwise report the hidden/unavailable panel as a display failure. Use presentation=now only for this turn's explicit show-now request; background skips presentation. Changed Tool descriptions and Skills require the host to refresh discovery before an existing chat can use them; API compatibility alone does not refresh its context. Verify actually loaded guidance, preserve data and project bindings, and report a stale chat without reinstalling or restarting unrelated work. During actual video generation and editing, do not mount any inline progress/video component and do not open the right editor for intermediate saves. Begin a business round silently with kinevyn_open_preview(action=begin,projectId,requestId,mode=create|modify); carry inlineWork.id as workId through saves and the final export. When the final authored video and assets are complete and ready to preview, prepare and present its editable Studio on the right. After the final MP4 export completes and passes technical verification, prefer the host-native video preview; Codex defaults to one video embed in the final reply without calling kinevyn_show_video. Only when native preview is unavailable, use the discovered kinevyn_show_video(projectId,workId) once instead. Never combine both previews for the same export; uncertain or pending presentation gets a plain file link, not a second player. Keep old final videos bound to their own immutable versions. Intermediate open/save/review/display operations never add a chat video frame. Explicit editor-only, show-now, background, unchanged-template and review requests retain their scope. The final playback needs no separate download request. Verify both the actual final player and editable Studio; neither replaces the other. For NEW generated media, use kinevyn_media_use inspect/reference/models to discover configured capabilities, then kinevyn_assets_use generate with the full model ID, status with the original jobId, get/read at a pinned assetId/versionId, and import_to_project only for selected film assets. No project is required for standalone generation. Use kinevyn_assets only when tools/list lacks the preferred name; it has no read, so inspect adopted local media with available tools. Keep old media_use jobs on their original Tool/projectId/jobId and never import their project files twice. Image references pin exact image versions: image models with supportsImageReference edit with up to their maxInputImages (one for local Codex and OpenDesign account models), and video models that report maxInputImages take one image as the first frame; first-and-last-frame video is unavailable. Recover failed or interrupted jobs with resume or retry_save as kinevyn://workflow/media/jobs describes; regeneration is a separate paid request requiring authorization. Follow the shared generation boundary in production/materials. Keep credentials in Settings, obtain missing spend consent, explain unsupported capabilities and proposed alternatives, and do not silently downgrade. Regenerate only within the asset count and spend the user explicitly approved, including any retries they approved; otherwise ask before another paid request; unknown outcomes require original-job inspection, not a new paid submission. Use kinevyn_project_archive to export explicit projectIds or all=true as an editable ZIP, or import a local ZIP sourcePath as independent copies. List projects with kinevyn_get_project first. Archive operations require a stable requestId; import never opens or overwrites an existing project. Use kinevyn_manage_project for info (saved title and local path), rename (expectedTitle and stable requestId), duplicate (stable requestId, optional title/revision) and reveal in the local file manager. Copies are independent and do not switch the editor. List Trash with kinevyn_get_project trashed=true. Use kinevyn_manage_project trash, restore or delete with an explicit projectId and stable requestId; delete requires a project already in Trash. For Design Studio HTML projects (prototype, deck, document, web-clone, live-artifact, webgl), read kinevyn://workflow/design/start and use kinevyn_design_catalog, kinevyn_design_project, kinevyn_design_edit (passing expectedRevision; every write creates a new version) and kinevyn_design_comments; call kinevyn_design_project action=open so the user can review and annotate in Design Studio.
